findings: ghd_02_19.tex:1047-1049 with :1042: 'always possible provided the property of global uniqueness holds' leaves implicit what the 4.77 construction uses at :1042 besides agreement of the solutions: Remark 4.67's agreement of the time orientations ('γ(t_{n0}) must also lie to the future of S in U_{α∞}'), stated under Thm 4.64's assumption that U₁ ∩ U₂ is connected. Agreement of the solutions gives one metric on the union but not, by itself, one time orientation on a component of an overlap that misses S. findings: ghd_02_19.tex:1063 ('The same argument as in the proof of Theorem 4.77 shows that u : U → R is a globally hyperbolic development') with :1042: the 4.77 argument invokes Remark 4.67 for the pair (U_{α_{n0}}, U_{α∞}), and Remark 4.67 is stated under the assumptions of Thm 4.64 (:915), U₁ ∩ U₂ connected. In 4.77 that connectedness is Lemma 4.70; for a pair of UGHDs ERS do not state it. It holds: in ERS's setting (subluminal, S connected and m-acausal, orientations by m) two GHDs that agree on their overlap have a connected overlap, by the argument of Lemma 4.72 with U₁'s g-Cauchy property and the agreement in place of U₁'s m-global hyperbolicity. (A point x of the overlap in J⁺(S, U₂) is in J⁺(S, U₁), else m-causal curves S → x → S contradict m-acausality; a past-inextendible g(u₂)-causal curve of U₂ from x meets S, and it cannot leave U₁ first, since its piece in U₁ ∩ U₂, where g(u₁) = g(u₂), would be a past-inextendible g(u₁)-causal curve of U₁ from a point of J⁺(S, U₁) and meet S before; so x is joined to S inside the overlap, which S connected makes connected.) Two UGHDs agree on their overlap, so Remark 4.67 does apply to them, and the gap at :1063 is only that this is not said. The Lean proof bypasses the question: S is acausal and ≤ antisymmetric in the whole union for g(v) by subluminality and Cm (Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_isAcausalOn). Correction of round 0 (AUDIT-1, major): the earlier text said that two UGHDs need not have a connected overlap; that is false in ERS's setting.

On ers_theorem_4_77's added hypothesis hcaus ('the union is causal', OQ-41 (d)): this observation leaves OQ-41 (d) open for Thm 4.77 itself, the superluminal theorem, where no Minkowski nesting is available. In 4.79 and 4.80 the corresponding statement is derived, not added: ≤ on the union is antisymmetric for g(v) by Causality.antisymm_of_curveNestedOn, from hsub and harc applied to the glued solution on the union (harc a named Lorentzian input: ≤ of g(v) realised by its causal curves) and Cm.IsCausal.

ghd_02_19.tex:1061: 'the domain of dependence of S in U₁ with respect to the Minkowski metric … gives rise to a m-GHD' also needs it to be a GHD for g(u₁), i.e. S a g(u₁)-Cauchy surface of it, left implicit; it holds because an inextendible g-causal curve is an inextendible m-causal curve. In ETT that is the localisation InextensibleNestedOn (OQ-41 (b)), not a consequence of curve nesting (kb/0045). The open set is the interior of D_m(S, U₁) (O'Neill 14.38).
questions: GHD read as 'S a Cauchy surface of U for g(u)', global hyperbolicity not concluded for the MUGHD (Geroch (iii) ⇒ (i) unproved), as OQ-57 (c) and OQ-41 (d) read it for 4.64 and 4.77. Is this acceptable for 4.79?

Subluminality read as curve nesting of g(u) in m for every solution, together with g(u) causally arc-connected on its domain (≤ realised by causal curves). The second is what makes S acausal and ≤ antisymmetric in the union. Is this pair the formalisation of record for 'subluminal'?
g(u, du) time-oriented by m (CausalityFollows: the causality is a function of the solution), in place of ERS's per-development stipulation that the normal of S is future directed. Acceptable reading?

'D_m(S) ∩ U₁ is an m-GHD' named as hDm (O'Neill 14.38, 14.43, the interior of the m-domain of dependence, the solution restricted) plus hinext (InextensibleNestedOn, OQ-41 (b)) for its g-Cauchy property. Is the split right, or should the whole be one named Minkowski fact?

readme_row: | `Causal.ErsMughd` | — | ETT programme, layer 1 (T-abs-ers-mughd): Eperon–Reall–Sbierski 1802.03020 Rem 4.78, Thms 4.79, 4.80 on a fixed background, the equation abstract (`sol`, `cau` with `SolutionLocal`, `SolutionsGlue`, `CausalityFollows`; `IsDevelopment`, `IsMDevelopment`, `IsUniqueDevelopment`): pairwise agreeing developments glue to a development under subluminality (`ers_remark_4_78`, by `Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_isAcausalOn`: S acausal in the union replaces Rem 4.67 and 4.77's added causality); every m-GHD is a UGHD through Cor 4.73 (`IsMDevelopment.isUniqueDevelopment`); the MUGHD (`ers_theorem_4_79`) and the unique m-MGHD (`ers_theorem_4_80`, `IsMaximalMDevelopment.unique`), contained in the MUGHD; `D_m(S) ∩ U₁` named (O'Neill 14.38, 14.43) with `InextensibleNestedOn`; nothing marked; 2026-11-21 |
kb_proposals: kb entry (pattern) 'Developments of one PDE on a fixed background, abstractly': Causal.IsDevelopment sol cau S U u (sol : Opens M → (M → β) → Prop with SolutionLocal, SolutionsGlue; cau : (M → β) → Causality M, the causality of g(u, du), with CausalityFollows), IsMDevelopment (m-Cauchy too), IsUniqueDevelopment (UGHD); a pairwise-agreeing family glues with exists_eqOn_of_pairwise, and its union is a development by ers_remark_4_78 under subluminality (T-abs-ers-mughd).

kb entry (pattern) 'A union of Cauchy open sets with S acausal in the union': Causal.Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_isAcausalOn needs no pairwise hypothesis (ers_theorem_4_77's hpair) and no ambient open (Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup of Causal.CBG.CausalConvex needs S Cauchy in an ambient B with CurvesExtendOn B); under subluminality its two hypotheses hold for g(u) on any domain: antisymm_of_curveNestedOn, isAcausalOn_of_curveNestedOn (curve_nested + causally_arc_connected on U, Cm causal, S m-acausal) (T-abs-ers-mughd).

kb note (pitfall) 'ers_theorem_4_77_greatest is not the set of developments': it is the greatest open set with S Cauchy for ONE causality, with no solution; for unions of developments carrying different causalities use ers_remark_4_78 (CausalityFollows transports the Cauchy property to the glued causality) (T-abs-ers-mughd).

label = "ersrem:RemMGHD"
ett = ["Causal.Causality.ers_theorem_4_77_greatest", "Causal.ers_remark_4_78", "Causal.exists_eqOn_of_pairwise", "Causal.Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_isAcausalOn"]

note = "Remark 4.78 (ghd_02_19.tex:1047): the union construction under global uniqueness. One-causality form ers_theorem_4_77_greatest (hpair, hcaus); subluminal form ers_remark_4_78 (T-abs-ers-mughd), its global uniqueness one function agreeing with every member, orientations by m."
